title: Ethiopian Split Pea Stew
community: All of Ethiopia — the spiced split pea wat
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Kik Wat — split peas cooked in a berbere sauce (unlike the mild Kik Alicha). The spiced, red version of the split pea stew — built on the same dry-caramelised onion base as Key Wat, but with peas instead of meat.
longDesc: Kik Wat is the spiced version of Kik Alicha — where Kik Alicha is mild and golden, Kik Wat is red and spiced with berbere. The split peas dissolve partially into the berbere sauce, producing a thick, rich stew that is as satisfying as Misir Wat.
ingredients: 2 cups green or yellow split peas — washed
steps: Add oil and berbere. Fry berbere 3 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger. Cook 1 minute.
chefTips: Split peas take longer to soften than red lentils — 40—45 minutes minimum.
The berbere base is identical to Misir Wat.
cookingScience: See ETH101 for berbere legume stew science. Split peas have a slightly higher starch content than red lentils — producing a thicker, more starchy sauce when dissolved.
sustainabilityTips: Split peas — very low environmental footprint.
culturalNote: Kik Wat is the spiced version of the split pea tradition — for those who want berbere heat in their legume stew. It sits naturally alongside Misir Wat on the fasting platter.
